speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing significant symptoms like fatigue, night sweats, weight loss, and an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node. To narrow this down, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits or appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The severity of your weight loss and "drenching" night sweats is concerning. Have you noticed any fever, cough, or bleeding gums recently? Also, have you had any difficulty swallowing food?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fact that the lymph node is "fixed" and non-tender, combined with your "drenching" night sweats and rapid weight loss, raises a strong suspicion for malignancy. Please tell me if you have experienced any skin rashes, itching, or jaundice, and REQUEST TEST: CBC, LDH, ESR, and Liver_Function_Tests.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count_WBC: Elevated, Complete_Blood_Count_Hemoglobin: Slightly Decreased, Complete_Blood_Count_Platelets: Normal, Lactate_Dehydrogenase: Elevated. (Note: ESR and Liver_Function_Tests were not included in the provided dataset.)

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma. Although the patient mentions a previous suspicion of Tuberculosis, the combination of a "fixed," non-tender supraclavicular lymph node, drenching night sweats, significant weight loss, and risk factors like smoking makes lymphoma the more likely primary diagnosis; please await the CBC and LDH results to confirm.
